mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% triggers market expectations of prolonged restrictive policy, which depresses risk asset valuations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of more than 0.5% in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based collapse in consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both fall > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 70% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 200,000 new jobs per month for four consecutive months signals a robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.6%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 97 for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of coordinated monetary easing.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes outside monetary easing.
